sections.content: You know *cuyo*, *cuya*, *cuyos* and *cuyas* from B1 Unit 5. They mean "whose" and agree with the noun that comes after them, not with the owner. They are useful for describing a network, a person or a find in a single sentence: *una red cuyo objetivo era…*, *los archivos, cuyo hallazgo…*

items.spanish: La Operación Cóndor fue una red cuyo objetivo era perseguir a los opositores.
items.english: Operation Condor was a network whose aim was to pursue opponents.

items.spanish: Letelier era un político cuya campaña contra Pinochet era muy conocida.
items.english: Letelier was a politician whose campaign against Pinochet was very well known.

items.spanish: Los archivos, cuyo hallazgo en 1992 cambió la investigación, mostraban la coordinación entre las policías.
items.english: The archives, whose discovery in 1992 changed the investigation, showed the coordination between the police forces.

items.spanish: Eran dictaduras cuyos servicios de inteligencia compartían información.
items.english: They were dictatorships whose intelligence services shared information.

sections.content: Do not put an article after *cuyo*: *cuyo objetivo*, not *cuyo el objetivo*. Do not replace it with *que su*: *una red que su objetivo era…* is a common mistake.
